deep.reconstruction:
Context: pages 33-35 classify the 'special' configurations (Sigma,K): Sigma is P^1 over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic 0 (or the complex sphere), K is a set of 5 points, and Aut(Sigma,K) is nontrivial. Let g be an automorphism of maximal order nu. A finite-order automorphism of P^1 has exactly two fixed points and acts freely off them, so K = K^g plus free orbits of size nu, with 2<=nu<=5. Page 33 handles three cases: nu=5 (pentagon, group D5), nu=4 (square pyramid, group Z/4), and nu=3 ('bitetrahedral' 0, infinity plus an equilateral triangle, group D3).

This page, case 4 (nu=2). Since |K| = 5 is odd and Sigma^g has two points, K^g = {P} is a single point. The remaining set I = K \ {P} is the union of two g-orbits of size 2. So g is the 'universal' involution of the 4-point configuration (Sigma, I), one of the three involutions in the Klein group V(Pi_I). P is one of the two fixed points of g.

Normal form. Take g(z) = -z, P = 0 (so infinity, the other fixed point, is not in K), and one orbit {+1,-1}. The other orbit is {t,-t}, with lambda = t^2 in k*, lambda != 1. Then K = {0, +-1, +-sqrt(lambda)}. Choosing the other orbit to normalise to +-1 replaces lambda by 1/lambda. The invariant parameter is rho = lambda + 1/lambda, with rho != 2. So this locus has one modulus ('cas moins intéressant ... car il y a des modules'). Its coarse moduli space is the rho-line minus the point rho = 2.

Grothendieck then places the special points of the earlier cases inside this family:
- When I is a 'square' structure (harmonic 4 points), either g is the half-turn preserving both diagonals and P is a pole; this is case 2°, with lambda = -1, rho = -2. Or I is an equatorial spherical square and P is the midpoint of an edge.
- He asks 'Est-ce le cas 1°?' about the edge-midpoint case.
- When I is tetrahedral, P is one of the 6 vertices of the associated octahedron (the fixed points of V4).

Second part: antiholomorphic automorphisms sigma of Sigma preserving K (k = C). Every orbit of a fixed-point-free antiholomorphic map of finite order (antipodal map, rotatory reflections) has even size. Since |K| = 5 is odd, sigma must fix a point of K. A finite-order antiholomorphic map with a fixed point is a reflection, so sigma has order 2 and is a real structure on Sigma. The cases are then split by |K^sigma| in {1,3,5}, which are treated on the next page. That page describes the real loci of M_{0,5}, each of real dimension 2, and counts cells. The whole purpose is to locate the remarkable points (points with symmetry) and the real structure of M_{0,5} and its S5-quotient, as base points and cells for the Teichmüller tower, i.e. the 'Lego' of the Esquisse.
errors: Correct but incomplete: no constraint is stated on lambda besides lambda != 0, 1. That is right: lambda = -1 is allowed and gives the square pyramid (case 2°, rho = -2), which is a point of the family with larger automorphism group.

His question 'Est-ce le cas 1°?' has a negative answer (my computation, not on the page). Take P = e^{i pi/4}, I = {+-1, +-i}, g(z) = i/z. This normalises to lambda = (tan(3pi/8)/tan(pi/8))^2 = 17+12sqrt2, so rho = 34. The pentagon (case 1°) gives lambda = (tan(2pi/5)/tan(pi/5))^2 = 9+4sqrt5, so rho = 18. The edge-midpoint configuration therefore has automorphism group exactly Z/2. V4 is excluded because it has no fixed point on Sigma.

Other special values (my computation): bitetrahedral case 3° gives lambda = -3, rho = -10/3; tetrahedral I with P an octahedron vertex gives lambda = -(7-4sqrt3), rho = -14. These are consistent with the remarks on the page; Grothendieck does not compute them.
The argument 'comme il est d'ordre pair, ... un point fixe au moins dans K' is terse, but it is correct for the reason given above (odd cardinality of K).

ideas.what: Classification of 5-point configurations on P^1 with nontrivial automorphism group; nu=2 case gives a one-parameter family K = {0, +-1, +-sqrt(lambda)} with invariant rho = lambda + 1/lambda
ideas.modern_name: Automorphism (stacky/orbifold) strata of M_{0,5}/S_5; locus of curves with an involution
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (finite subgroups of PGL2, Klein); orbifold structure of M_{0,n}/S_n is standard folklore
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses M_{0,4}, M_{0,5}, points with symmetry and the Teichmüller tower in general terms; no explicit classification of this kind that I know of

ideas.what: Interpreting the involution as an element of the Klein four-group of the 4-point configuration I, with P one of the 6 fixed points of V4 (octahedron vertices in the tetrahedral case)
ideas.modern_name: Klein 4-group action on 4-point configurations / Legendre family symmetries

ideas.what: Antiholomorphic automorphisms preserving K are reflections; real structures classified by |K^sigma| in {1,3,5}, giving real loci of M_{0,5}
ideas.modern_name: Real points / real forms of M_{0,5} (cell decomposition by associahedra, real-locus components)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Real locus of M_{0,n}: Kapranov, Devadoss, Etingof-Henriques-Kamnitzer-Rains (cell structure); classical for small n
ideas.where_published: Esquisse mentions real structures and cell decompositions of modular multiplicities in general

missed.claim: Grothendieck leaves open whether the 'equatorial square plus edge-midpoint' configuration coincides with the pentagonal case. It does not: rho = 34 versus 18. He also does not record where the special symmetric points lie on the rho-line (-2, -10/3, 18, plus the remarkable non-extra-symmetric values 34 and -14). This is minor and easily computed today; it is not a significant gap in the literature.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: These are explicit coordinates of the orbifold points of M_{0,5}/S_5 on the involution curve, which are useful as base points or paths in Grothendieck-Teichmüller and Lego computations. The material is elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an elementary, careful case analysis of the automorphism strata of 5 points on P^1 and their real structures, written as groundwork for the Teichmüller tower. The content is classical or routine; its only interest is documenting Grothendieck's hands-on study of the symmetric points of M_{0,5}.
transcription_corrections: 'Les deux K^g={P}' should read just 'K^g = {P}' (the insertion above the line is likely 'Ici, dans' or similar, not 'Les deux').
'donc lambda = J=(0,+-1,+-sqrt(lambda))' should read 'donc K = (0,+-1,+-sqrt(lambda))'; the J is presumably K.
'lambda in Z(lambda) - {0,1,infty}' is probably 'lambda in P^1(k) - {0,1,infty}' or 'Sigma(k) - {0,1,infty}'.
'Cas moins intéressant que les précédents, du moins pour des uns' should probably read 'du moins pour nous' / 'pour ce qui nous occupe'.

'soit le cas des sommets d'un carré sphériques équatoriaux et des milieux des arêtes' should read 'soit le cas où I est formé des sommets d'un carré sphérique équatorial et P un des milieux des arêtes'.
'Cas des antiautomorphismes sigma de Sigma laissant stables K' is correct; the marginal note reads '(Cas k = C)'.
